text:
The Flyers beat Vancouver 5-2 last night without Matvei Michkov, and the win was not the main topic afterward. Michkov sat out with no injury listed; Sean Couturier said the team found out before the game, and both he and Travis Konecny were careful with their words, per Charlie O'Connor of PHLY Sports. Rick Tocchet's answer on the follow-up was short, as O'Connor posted it: "Tocchet says Michkov will be in the lineup tomorrow." So he plays tonight, in a week when Konecny's name is also in trade chatter, with Markerzone reporting the Flyers will listen on him. Philadelphia is 4-1-0 in its last five, but its season-long share of five-on-five expected goals, the quality of chances, is just 44%.

The Islanders arrive with a different kind of question. They are 29 points into the season with a +5 goal difference, on chances that say they should be 10.9 goals worse. The gap has a name: Ilya Sorokin, projected to start, at 10.9 goals saved above expected and a .916 save percentage. That is how a team survives losing the shot battle, and it is also how a record can wobble when the goalie is merely good.

Kyle Palmieri's knee injury, with ESPN estimating a return in June, has reshuffled the forwards. Mathew Barzal moved back beside Bo Horvat and is up to 22 minutes a night, and Pete DeBoer has kept tinkering, per NHL.com's Stefen Rosner. Matthew Schaefer, last year's first overall pick and already the face of the team, has been "human these last five or so games," as Rosner put it. He is still our likeliest Islander for two points tonight at 35%.

Both teams played last night, so expect tired legs on both benches. The Islanders managed only 26% of the expected goals in their 3-1 loss to Winnipeg, which is the number Sorokin will be leaning against again.
headline: Michkov returns to a Flyers room with questions
